inputClassification: Category 3: Local civil timestamp with user-specified numerical timezone offset

missingTimezoneCases.finding: Calling generateKundali with non-numeric timezone propagates NaN into dateToJD and RASHIS indexing, causing TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'en').
missingTimezoneCases.recommendedSafeHandling: Input validation in public API: if (typeof timezone !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(timezone)) throw new TypeError('Invalid timezone specified'); or fallback to longitude / 15.0 for LMT.

conceptualProof.premise: Does a Delta-T polynomial perform local-time-to-UT1 conversion?
conceptualProof.proof: Delta-T is defined astronomically as TT - UT1. It accounts exclusively for the Earth's rotational deceleration relative to atomic/dynamical clocks. The conversion from Local Civil Time to Greenwich Mean Time (UT1/UTC) is performed strictly by subtracting the geographical/civil timezone offset (or longitude in hours for Local Mean Time). Applying Delta-T to uncorrected local clock time would erroneously confuse geographical longitude offset with Earth deceleration.
